common_name: Prince Jacob's Ladder (Compact Blue-Flowered Shade Polemonium)

planting.note: Set divisions or container plants out in spring once soil has warmed, into humus-rich, evenly moist ground in a woodland border or shaded bed.

directions: Prince forms a dense, compact mound of finely divided, fern-like foliage that stays ornamental well beyond the bloom period. Clear blue flowers rise above the foliage in spring and continue into summer, each held in a purple calyx that remains attractive on the plant even after petals drop. The foliage itself takes on purple tints in spring and again in fall, adding a second season of color in a shaded border. It suits woodland gardens, mixed shade borders, or path edges where its tidy habit and long bloom window can be appreciated up close.

common_name: Grand Teton Hellebore (Rockies Series Burgundy-Flowered Shade Hybrid)

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall into rich, well-drained soil beneath deciduous trees or shrubs, where winter sun can reach the clump before leaf-out.

directions: Grand Teton is part of the Rockies series of compact, mounded hellebores bred by Miyoko Hattori in Japan for architectural evergreen foliage alongside persistent flowers. New growth emerges a smoky grey-blue with slender, spine-tipped leaflets, setting off the dark burgundy blooms that open in spring and are accented by bright yellow reflexed anthers. The flowers hold their color and shape on the plant for an extended period rather than fading quickly, keeping the display going well past typical hellebore bloom windows. Site in a part-shade to shaded bed with reliable moisture to keep the low, dense mound looking full through the season.

common_name: Mount Nebo Hellebore (Rockies Series Variegated Pink-Blushed Shade Hybrid)

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall into rich, well-drained soil beneath deciduous trees or shrubs, where winter sun can reach the clump before leaf-out.

directions: Mount Nebo stands out among the Rockies series hellebores for foliage that emerges bright red in fall and again in early spring before settling into a speckled pattern of pink, white, and green. Rosy pink buds open into flowers that hold their blush color for weeks before slowly shifting toward chartreuse as they age, giving the clump a long, gradually changing floral display. The combination of colorful new growth and long-lasting flowers makes it useful as a season-spanning focal point in a shaded bed rather than a plant valued for bloom alone. Grow in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in part to full shade and avoid letting the root zone dry out during establishment.

common_name: Hollowtop Mountain Hellebore (Rockies Series White-Veined Shade Hybrid)

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall into rich, well-drained soil beneath deciduous trees or shrubs, where winter sun can reach the clump before leaf-out.

directions: Hollowtop Mountain is grown chiefly for its patterned evergreen foliage, with fall and early-spring leaves marked by bright white midveins and marbling that develop reddish petioles as the plant matures. Single, clear white flowers open in early spring ahead of most of the Rockies series and gradually take on a rosy flush as they age. The strong foliage contrast keeps the clump visually interesting through the dormant season, well before and after the comparatively brief bloom period. Site in part to full shade with consistently moist, fertile soil to maintain the crisp leaf variegation.

common_name: Pike's Peak Hellebore (Rockies Series Silver-Leaved Sternii Hybrid)
scientific_name: Helleborus x sternii x argutifolius 'Pike's Peak' PP36018

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall into gritty, well-drained soil beneath deciduous trees or shrubs, where winter sun can reach the clump before leaf-out.

directions: Pike's Peak was bred by Miyoko Hattori from a cross between Helleborus x sternii and H. argutifolius, and it shows that parentage in jagged, silvery-grey leaflets with finely toothed margins that give the clump a spiky, textured look year-round. Clusters of chartreuse flowers open in spring and persist on the plant for an extended period rather than dropping quickly, adding soft color against the metallic foliage. Because of its argutifolius and sternii ancestry it tolerates somewhat drier, better-drained sites than typical Lenten rose hybrids. Grow in part shade with sharply drained soil to keep the silvery foliage from declining in wet winters.

common_name: Snowshoe Mountain Hellebore (Rockies Series Green-Speckled Shade Hybrid)

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall into rich, well-drained soil beneath deciduous trees or shrubs, where winter sun can reach the clump before leaf-out.

directions: Snowshoe Mountain opens its flowers earlier than most of the Rockies series, often in late winter, with rose-blushed buds that mature to blooms freckled with green before slowly fading toward solid green. New foliage emerges with a rosy tinge and matures into leaves speckled in white and green, echoing the color shifts seen in the flowers. The long-blooming flowers and patterned leaves combine to give the clump visual interest from the last weeks of winter well into spring. Plant in part to full shade in evenly moist, humus-rich soil for the best foliage color.

common_name: Table Mountain Hellebore (Rockies Series Gold-Foliage Purple-Flowered Shade Hybrid)
scientific_name: Helleborus argutifolius x lividus 'Table Mountain' PP35771

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall into rich, well-drained soil beneath deciduous trees or shrubs, where winter sun can reach the clump before leaf-out.

directions: Table Mountain is grown as much for its foliage as its flowers, with new leaves emerging in a swirled mix of green and gold that brightens to a strong gold tone with contrasting purple petioles as the season progresses. Rosy purple blooms open in spring and persist on the plant, gradually fading to a dusty rose brushed with chartreuse at the base of each petal. Bred by Miyoko Hattori from a Helleborus argutifolius x lividus cross made in Tokyo, the gold foliage reads as a bright accent in a shaded bed long after the flowers have faded, making this cultivar useful for extending seasonal interest. Grow in part to full shade with consistently moist, fertile soil to keep the gold coloring from scorching.
